newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag eases despite strong 1996 figures.
newsitem.headline: Viag eases despite strong 1996 figures.

text.p: Shares in German diversified utility Viag AG eased slightly in pre-bourse trade on Friday despite reporting figures that were generally seen to be in line, or even slightly better than expected.

Analysts and dealers said however that the stock was suffering from a degree of volatility and profit-taking at the moment related to overly-optimistic profit expectations among some investors in the German utility sector.
"It looks now that following the Viag figures the market's wildest hopes on profits will turn to Veba," said one dealer. Utility Veba was traded slightly higher, in line with the market.
Earlier Viag reported 1996 group sales up at 42.5 billion marks from 41.9 billion and a group operating profit before tax of just under 2.4 billion compared to 2.1 billion in 1995.
